entries.question: When Markus freed the three androids in the crate (FREE THEM), did a Jericho arrow appear along with the North, Simon and Josh arrows?
entries.why: template gives North/Simon/Josh only on the drone, FREE THEM and ACCEPT although it tags Jericho elsewhere in the chapter; wiki (Jericho list lines 100-104) and PowerPyx ('North▲, Jericho▲, Josh▲, Simon▲' on freeing) add Jericho up/down; the reliability log has the template wrong twice on arrows. One answer settles all three moments. Benchmark applies no Jericho arrow (up to +3/-1 Jericho at stake)

entries.topic: Control-room alarm and BACK TO JERICHO
originals: The edges out of the two RUN TO FENCE nodes
After a control-room alarm, are the only outcomes the dogs and Markus's damage, or can the group reach BACK TO JERICHO?
entries.question: After the guards raised the alarm in the control room, did the group ever get over the fence without the dogs catching John?
entries.why: lines at the SUSTAIN DAMAGE junction cross in sp-7.jpg; the wiki nests 'Back to Jericho > Group Failed Their Mission OR Group Returned With Full Bags' under Fail to Avoid Guards > Run to Fence; benchmark gives only dogs (M05n) or damage, so John always dies after a control-room alarm

originals: Can Markus be damaged at the fence when no alarm has sounded (after LEAVE)?
entries.question: After LEAVE at the truck-key question (no alarm), could Markus still be too slow at the fence and get damaged?
entries.why: the template files the fence 'Take too much time' under '## Was detected by the guards - Running away'; the chart's lower RUN TO FENCE (fed by both the alarm and LEAVE) has an uncertain edge to SUSTAIN DAMAGE REACHING THE FENCE; benchmark rolls 0.08 for failure after LEAVE

originals: Can SAVE ever save John? (§8 item 4)
Can SAVE ever save John? (recap)
entries.answer: No. The 100% chart's DOGS MAUL JOHN group holds only LEAVE JOHN BEHIND and SUSTAIN DAMAGE TRYING TO SAVE JOHN (> GROUP FAILED THEIR MISSION), and the John page says he 'dies regardless if Markus chooses to go back for him or leave'
entries.source: sp-7.jpg; /tmp/flowcharts/ch19/wiki.txt lines 72-77; research note §4 quoting the John page

originals: HIDE and the failed ending
HIDE takes the "Ran away when the guard arrived" ending block, like RUN AWAY
Does HIDE give the same Jericho ending block as RUN AWAY?
entries.answer: Yes. The chart sends HIDE along the same bottom line as RUN AWAY to the lower ALARM SOUNDS; the template's HIDE ends with 'Hit the fucking alarm!' before the bags are filled; PowerPyx: HIDE 'ends in the team running away and ending the mission early'. The only template block for that run is 'Ran away when the guard arrived'
entries.source: sp-4.jpg (group ATTACK / GRAB / RUN AWAY / HIDE); transcript.txt lines 49-52 and In Jericho block; wiki.txt line 44 ('Hide - leads to Alarm Sounds')

entries.topic: TRIGGER ALARM carries the seen-by-guards arrows
originals: The "Be seen by the guards" arrows also apply on TRIGGER ALARM
Does TRIGGER ALARM carry the "Be seen by the guards" arrows? Can Markus be seen after taking the key
Which control-room failures carry the "Be seen by the guards" icons?
entries.answer: Yes for TRIGGER ALARM: it is a failure to get the key followed by the run to the fence, and the wiki ties the North double down to exactly that ('Running to the fence after failing to get the key' x2; Notes: 'If Markus fails to get the key, Markus' relationship with North decreases twice'). The template's 'Threaten guards with the gun' block is empty, so it adds nothing on top. Being seen after taking the key is an unmodelled rare path (see ch19-14)
entries.source: transcript.txt 'Be seen by the guards' block; wiki.txt lines 105, 119 and Notes
